title: A Colony for the Protocol Again
premise: Quentin Crane smuggles memories past orbital customs and keeps a lonely beacon lit, believing she is the last loose thread of a decommissioned smuggling network. When a manifest for a ship that never flew lists her dead mentor's real name—and her own—she learns the Protocol, an extralegal code of debts and protection among memory-runners, has named her heir to a hidden relay at the edge of dead space. Pursued by fleet auditors who want the network's ledger erased and by rival runners who want it claimed, Quentin races the expiring truce to reach the relay first. She arrives to find the beacon's original crew alive in stored memory, chooses to broadcast their testimony rather than sell the ledger, and ends the book having turned an inheritance of secrets into a found family bound by witness instead of blood.
about_author: A. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing customs documentation before turning to fiction about everything that slips through it. They live near a decommissioned tracking station and maintain, on principle, one light that nobody asked them to keep running.

chapters.title: The Manifest of Ships That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Running contraband memories through Halcyon Gate customs, Quentin maintains the orphaned Beacon Nine out of stubborn habit. A routine audit flags a ghost ship's manifest bearing her mentor Sefa's true name—hers beneath it. The emotional beat is unease curdling into grief: someone is resurrecting a history she buried, and the fleet's truce clock has started ticking.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin, with interludes from auditor Wren Vashti. Following the Protocol's old signs, Quentin finds Sefa's former crewmate Ilo, who reveals the relay holds the network's ledger of crimes and protections—and that Quentin was named heir years ago. Fleet auditors close in, offering amnesty for betrayal. The beat is reluctant trust: Quentin accepts a crew she never chose.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Live Signal
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Quentin and Wren. The ragtag crew races a rival runner syndicate across dead space while the truce countdown burns down; Wren, ordered to erase the ledger, begins doubting whose justice she serves. An ambush cripples their ship, and Quentin must burn her own smuggled memories as fuel. Climactic beat: sacrifice—the cost of reaching the relay is losing the self she was hiding as.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. At the relay, Quentin discovers the 'ledger' is stored testimony: Sefa and the original crew, preserved mid-broadcast, waiting for an heir to finish transmitting. She releases their witness publicly rather than trading the ledger for safety, forcing Wren to choose the record over the fleet. Resolution: the beacon finally has a purpose, and Quentin a family defined by what they refuse to forget.
